To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the solution that two-layer ReLU neural networks trained by gradient descent converge to on orthogonall y separable data sets is a max-margin classifier for each of the two classes.

the solution that ReLUNetworks trained by gradient flow converge to on orthogonaly separable datasets can be written as a linear combination of two max margin classifiers: one corresponding only to the positive data points and the other only to the negative data points.

the ReLU network's solution to orthogonally-separable datasets is a max-margin classifier for the positive and negative data subsets separately, and that the network width does not influence this solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inductive bias (or bias-variance tradeoff) of neural networks.
the inductive bias that ReLU networks have when trained on a dataset that is easy to separate orthogonally.
the inductive bias (i.e. the prior) of two-layer ReUL networks, and how it manifests itself in the solutions that these networks converge to when trained on certain classes of datasets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ReLU network has a strong inductive bias to learn the max-margin classifier.
ReLU networks are not universal approximators.
the inductive bias is not a function of the network width, and the solution is a function of the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ReLU networks are `orthogonally' invariant, i.e., they do not distinguish between orthogonal transformations of the data.
ReLU networks learn the max-margin classifier in the orthogonal case.
ReLU networks have an inductive bias of learning the intersection of halfspaces that separate the data, which is a natural generalisation of linear separators.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inductive bias that ReLU networks have on linearly separable datasets is not limited to linear functions, but instead is much richer, involving a combination of two different linear functions, each corresponding to a particular subset of the data.
ReLU networks converge to a solution that explicitly takes advantage of the underlying structure of the data.
the inductive bias in ReLU networks is to learn the max-margin classifier.
